subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare the Mauryan period and the Gupta period: one difference in language or writing, and one in what they are best remembered for.
prompt_hi: Maurya kaal aur Gupta kaal ki tulna karo: bhasha ya lekhan mein ek fark, aur ve sabse zyada kis liye yaad kiye jaate hain usmein ek fark.
answer: Mauryas: edicts mostly in Prakrit (Brahmi script); remembered for a huge empire and Ashoka's dhamma. Guptas: courtly works mostly in Sanskrit; remembered for science, mathematics, literature, art and temples.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why did so much creativity happen in the Gupta period? Give three reasons.
prompt_hi: Gupta kaal mein itni rachnaatmakta kyun hui? 3 kaaran batao.
answer: Kings and rich patrons supported scholars, poets and artists; wealth from farming and trade paid for buildings, art and learning; relative peace in the core regions; centres of learning like Nalanda where scholars could study and teach.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Was the Gupta period a "golden age" for everyone? Compare how a court poet and a farmer might have described their lives.
prompt_hi: Kya Gupta kaal sabke liye "swarn yug" tha? Ek darbaari kavi aur ek kisaan apni zindagi ka varnan kaise karte — tulna karo.
answer: A court poet, supported by the king, might describe wealth, beauty and learning. A farmer might describe hard work, taxes and dependence on rain. Most surviving sources come from courts and elites, so "golden age" fits some groups better than others; historians weigh both views.

subject: sst
prompt_en: A timeline shows: c. 320 CE Chandragupta I; c. 335 CE Samudragupta; c. 400 CE Faxian visits; 499 CE the Aryabhatiya is written. Tell this story in two sentences, in order, and say roughly how many years pass from the first mark to the last.
prompt_hi: Ek timeline par hai: lagbhag 320 CE Chandragupta I; lagbhag 335 CE Samudragupta; lagbhag 400 CE Faxian aate hain; 499 CE Aryabhatiya likhi jaati hai. Yeh kahaani do vaakyon mein kram se batao, aur pehle se aakhri nishaan tak lagbhag kitne saal hue?
answer: Chandragupta I began the Guptas' rise around 320 CE, and his son Samudragupta expanded the kingdom from about 335 CE. Around 400 CE the Chinese traveller Faxian visited, and in 499 CE Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya — about 180 years after the first mark.

subject: sst
prompt_en: India's first satellite, launched in 1975, was named Aryabhata. Why might scientists have chosen that name? Where do you use a place-value number system in your own day?
prompt_hi: India ka pehla satellite, jo 1975 mein chhoda gaya, uska naam Aryabhata rakha gaya. Vaigyanikon ne yeh naam kyun chuna hoga? Apne din mein tum place-value wali sankhya pranaali kahan use karte ho?
answer: To honour an Indian pioneer of astronomy and mathematics. Place value is used everywhere: prices, phone numbers, cricket scores, page numbers, money (in 305, the 3 means 3 hundreds and the 0 holds the tens place).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if kings and rich patrons had stopped supporting poets, scholars and artists, what would have happened to Gupta-era creativity?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar raja aur ameer sanrakshak kaviyon, vidvaanon aur kalakaaron ki madad karna band kar dete, toh Gupta kaal ki rachnaatmakta ka kya hota?
answer: Much less would have been created: scholars and artists need time, materials and a living to write books, paint caves or build temples; without patronage many would have had to do other work, so fewer works of science, art and literature would have been made or preserved.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend why the Gupta period is called an age of tireless creativity: give one example each from science, art and literature, and one caution historians add.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki Gupta kaal ko "athak rachnaatmakta ka yug" kyun kehte hain: vigyan, kala aur sahitya se ek-ek example do, aur ek saavdhani jo itihaaskar jodte hain.
answer: Key idea: science — Aryabhata (Earth's rotation, eclipses, pi) or the rust-resistant iron pillar; art — early stone temples (e.g. Deogarh) or the Ajanta cave paintings of the same period (made under the Vakatakas, Gupta allies); literature — Kalidasa's Shakuntalam or Meghaduta; caution — sources mainly show courts and elites, so it was not golden for everyone.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why might a sangam — a place where rivers meet — be seen as especially sacred?
prompt_hi: Sangam — jahan nadiyaan milti hain — ko khaas taur par pavitra kyun maana ja sakta hai?
answer: Rivers give water, food and life; where two or more meet, the meeting of life-giving waters feels powerful and special, and such places became natural gathering points for people, rituals and fairs (like the Kumbh at Prayagraj).

subject: sst
prompt_en: The Char Dham are at four corners of India. Name each and say in which direction and state it lies. What does visiting all four suggest?
prompt_hi: Char Dham Bharat ke chaar konon par hain. Har ek ka naam, disha aur rajya batao. Chaaron ki yatra karna kya dikhata hai?
answer: Badrinath – north (Uttarakhand); Dwarka – west (Gujarat); Puri – east (Odisha); Rameswaram – south (Tamil Nadu). Visiting all four means crossing the whole land, which expresses the idea that the whole of India is one connected sacred land.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name the four places where the Kumbh Mela is held, with the river at each.
prompt_hi: Kumbh Mela jin chaar jagahon par lagta hai unke naam aur wahan ki nadi batao.
answer: Prayagraj (confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna, with the Saraswati of tradition), Haridwar (Ganga), Ujjain (Shipra), Nashik (Godavari).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Match each place with the tradition for which it is most famous: Bodh Gaya, Shravanabelagola, Golden Temple (Amritsar), Ajmer Sharif, Velankanni.
prompt_hi: Har jagah ko us parampara se milao jiske liye woh sabse prasiddh hai: Bodh Gaya, Shravanabelagola, Swarn Mandir (Amritsar), Ajmer Sharif, Velankanni.
answer: Bodh Gaya – Buddhist (Buddha's enlightenment); Shravanabelagola – Jain (Gommateshwara statue); Golden Temple – Sikh; Ajmer Sharif – Sufi shrine (dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti), visited by people of many faiths; Velankanni – Christian (basilica in Tamil Nadu).

subject: sst
prompt_en: How did pilgrimage connect different parts of India long ago?
prompt_hi: Puraane samay mein teerth yatra ne Bharat ke alag-alag hisson ko kaise joda?
answer: Pilgrims travelled long distances, met people of other regions, shared stories, songs, languages and food, and traders and artisans followed the routes; this created links and a shared sense of belonging across the land.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: if all long pilgrimage routes had closed for a hundred years, what might have happened to the links between regions?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar saare lambe teerth raaste sau saal ke liye band ho jaate, toh kshetron ke beech ke rishton ka kya hota?
answer: Fewer people would travel between regions, so there would be less sharing of languages, stories, crafts, food and trade, and regions might feel more separate from each other.

subject: sst
prompt_en: How do sacred groves help nature?
prompt_hi: Pavitra upvan (sacred groves) prakriti ki madad kaise karte hain?
answer: Because communities believe the grove is sacred, they do not cut its trees or hunt there; so the groves protect old trees, springs, birds, animals and medicinal plants, and keep soil and water healthy — like small forest reserves kept by tradition.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Is there a place near your home that people treat as sacred or special — a tree, a pond, a hill, a shrine? How do people care for it, and how could you help keep it clean?
prompt_hi: Kya tumhare ghar ke paas koi aisi jagah hai jise log pavitra ya khaas maante hain — koi ped, talaab, pahadi, ya sthaan? Log uski dekhbhaal kaise karte hain, aur tum use saaf rakhne mein kaise madad kar sakte ho?
answer: A good answer names a real local place, describes a practice of care (not cutting the tree, cleaning festivals, rules about waste) and suggests a realistic action (not littering, joining a clean-up, using cloth bags, reminding visitors).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare a sacred river site (like the ghats at Haridwar) with a sacred grove (like a kavu in Kerala): what is sacred, how people use it, and how it affects nature.
prompt_hi: Ek pavitra nadi sthal (jaise Haridwar ke ghaat) aur ek pavitra upvan (jaise Kerala ka kavu) ki tulna karo: kya pavitra hai, log ise kaise use karte hain, aur prakriti par kya asar padta hai.
answer: River site: the flowing river is sacred; huge numbers of pilgrims bathe and perform rituals; crowds can cause pollution unless managed. Sacred grove: the forest itself is sacred; few people enter and rules forbid cutting; it protects trees, wildlife and water. Both show nature being revered.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistake: "Pilgrims in old India only visited places in their own village, so pilgrimage never connected different regions."
prompt_hi: Galti pakdo: "Puraane Bharat mein yatri sirf apne gaon ki jagahon par jaate the, isliye teerth yatra ne kabhi alag kshetron ko nahi joda."
answer: Pilgrims often travelled hundreds or thousands of kilometres — Kashi to Rameswaram, Kerala to Badrinath — so pilgrimage strongly connected distant regions through shared travel, culture and trade.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Many sacred rivers today are polluted. Give two causes and two solutions.
prompt_hi: Aaj kai pavitra nadiyaan pradooshit hain. Do kaaran aur do samaadhaan batao.
answer: Causes: untreated sewage and factory waste, plastic and puja waste thrown in, too much water taken out. Solutions: treat sewage before it enters rivers, stop plastic and dispose of offerings properly, clean-up drives, laws against factory dumping, keeping ghats clean.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a friend how "the land becomes sacred" in India and why this matters for India's unity. Use two examples from different traditions.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki Bharat mein "zameen pavitra kaise banti hai" aur yeh Bharat ki ekta ke liye kyun mahatvapoorn hai. Do alag paramparaon se example do.
answer: Key idea: people link natural features or events with the sacred (e.g. the Ganga and the Kumbh; Bodh Gaya where the Buddha attained enlightenment; the Golden Temple; Velankanni); pilgrims travel across regions to these places, creating connections, shared culture and respect among many communities.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Mount Kailash is regarded as sacred by which traditions?
prompt_hi: Kailash parvat ko kaun-kaun si paramparaayein pavitra maanti hain?
answer: Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, and followers of the Bon tradition of Tibet.

subject: sst
prompt_en: What would happen in a cricket match with no rules and no umpire? How is that like a country without a government?
prompt_hi: Bina niyam aur bina umpire ke cricket match mein kya hoga? Yeh bina sarkaar wale desh jaisa kaise hai?
answer: Players would argue, the strongest would get their way and the game might break down; similarly, without a government and rules, there would be no fair way to decide, settle quarrels or keep people safe.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name four types of government.
prompt_hi: Chaar tarah ki sarkaaron ke naam batao.
answer: Monarchy, democracy, dictatorship, theocracy (also oligarchy).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name the type of government in each: (a) a king decides everything and cannot be questioned; (b) citizens elect leaders every five years; (c) a leader took power by force and bans criticism; (d) religious leaders rule by religious law; (e) a queen is head of state but an elected parliament makes laws.
prompt_hi: Har ek mein sarkaar ka prakaar batao: (a) raja sab kuch tay karta hai aur us par sawaal nahi uthaya ja sakta; (b) naagrik har paanch saal mein neta chunte hain; (c) ek neta ne taaqat se satta li aur aalochna par rok lagaayi; (d) dharmik neta dharmik kaanoon se raaj karte hain; (e) rani rajya ki pramukh hai par chuni hui sansad kaanoon banati hai.
answer: (a) absolute monarchy; (b) representative democracy; (c) dictatorship; (d) theocracy; (e) constitutional monarchy.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare monarchy and democracy: how is the leader chosen, and can people remove the leader?
prompt_hi: Raajtantra aur loktantra ki tulna karo: neta kaise chuna jaata hai, aur kya log use hata sakte hain?
answer: Monarchy: the ruler gets the position by birth, usually for life, and people cannot vote them out (in an absolute monarchy). Democracy: leaders are elected by the people for a fixed term and can be voted out at the next election.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Compare direct democracy (as in ancient Athens) with representative democracy (as in India). Why can't India use direct democracy for every decision?
prompt_hi: Pratyaksh loktantra (jaise puraane Athens mein) aur pratinidhi loktantra (jaise Bharat mein) ki tulna karo. Bharat har faisle ke liye pratyaksh loktantra kyun nahi apna sakta?
answer: Direct: citizens themselves meet and vote on each decision. Representative: citizens elect representatives (MLAs, MPs) who make decisions for them. India has over a billion people, so they cannot all meet and vote on every law; electing representatives makes decisions possible.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Is voting enough to make a country a democracy? Explain.
prompt_hi: Kya sirf voting se koi desh loktantra ban jaata hai? Samjhao.
answer: No. Voting matters, but a democracy also needs equal rights, freedom of speech and a free press, independent courts, the rule of law that applies to leaders too, and protection for minorities, so people can question and check those in power.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistake: "In a democracy, once people have voted, leaders can do anything they like until the next election."
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondho: "Loktantra mein ek baar vote dene ke baad neta agle chunaav tak jo chahein kar sakte hain."
answer: Leaders in a democracy must follow the constitution and laws; courts can strike down unlawful actions; the press, the opposition and citizens can question them; they remain accountable all the time, not only at elections.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict: what might happen in a country if newspapers and people were not allowed to criticise the government?
prompt_hi: Socho: agar kisi desh mein akhbaar aur log sarkaar ki aalochna nahi kar sakte, toh kya ho sakta hai?
answer: Mistakes and wrongdoing by those in power could stay hidden; people would not know the truth or be able to demand change; leaders could become more powerful and less accountable, moving towards dictatorship.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Your class must choose a picnic spot. Design a democratic way to decide that also respects the few students who disagree.
prompt_hi: Tumhari class ko picnic ki jagah chunni hai. Faisla karne ka ek loktantrik tareeka banao jo un kuch bachchon ka bhi samman kare jo sahmat nahi hain.
answer: For example: everyone can suggest options; each option is discussed openly; everyone gets one equal vote (secret ballot); the majority choice wins; the minority's concerns (cost, food, distance, disability access) are listened to and addressed; nobody is punished for disagreeing.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Diagram A shows arrows from "citizens" up to "parliament" and then to "prime minister". Diagram B shows arrows only from "king" down to "everyone". Describe each diagram in words and name the type of government.
prompt_hi: Diagram A mein teer "naagrik" se "sansad" tak aur phir "pradhan mantri" tak jaate hain. Diagram B mein teer sirf "raja" se neeche "sab" ki taraf jaate hain. Har diagram ko shabdon mein samjhao aur sarkaar ka prakaar batao.
answer: A: power flows up from the citizens, who elect parliament, which chooses the prime minister — a representative (parliamentary) democracy. B: power flows down from the king to everyone, who cannot choose him — an absolute monarchy.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Teach a younger sibling how a democracy is different from a dictatorship, using an example from your family or school.
prompt_hi: Chhote bhai-behen ko ghar ya school ka example le kar samjhao ki loktantra taanashahi se kaise alag hai.
answer: Key idea: in a democracy people choose leaders, can speak freely, and leaders follow the rules and can be changed (like a class electing a monitor who can be replaced); in a dictatorship one person takes control, makes all rules and cannot be questioned or removed.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why can't a majority in a democracy simply vote to take away the basic rights of a smaller group?
prompt_hi: Loktantra mein bahumat kisi chhote samooh ke mool adhikaar vote se kyun nahi chheen sakta?
answer: Because in a constitutional democracy like India, fundamental rights belong to every person and are protected by the constitution; courts can strike down laws that violate them. Democracy means rule by the people with rights for all, not rule by the majority alone.

subject: sst
prompt_en: When was the Constitution adopted, and when did it come into force? Which days do we celebrate for each?
prompt_hi: Samvidhan kab apnaya gaya aur kab laagu hua? Har ek ke liye hum kaunsa din manaate hain?
answer: Adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas); came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

subject: sst
prompt_en: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly, and who chaired its Drafting Committee?
prompt_hi: Samvidhan Sabha ke Adhyaksh kaun the, aur Praaroop (Drafting) Samiti ke adhyaksh kaun the?
answer: Dr Rajendra Prasad was President of the Constituent Assembly; Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Make a word timeline: the Constituent Assembly first meets (9 December 1946); the Constitution is adopted (26 November 1949); it comes into force (26 January 1950). Describe it in sentences and say roughly how long the Assembly took to finish.
prompt_hi: Shabdon wali timeline banao: Samvidhan Sabha ki pehli baithak (9 December 1946); Samvidhan apnaya gaya (26 November 1949); laagu hua (26 January 1950). Ise vaakyon mein batao aur lagbhag kitna samay laga, yeh bhi batao.
answer: The Assembly first met in December 1946, debated for almost three years (about 2 years 11 months), adopted the Constitution in November 1949, and it came into force two months later in January 1950.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Name the four ideals the Preamble aims to secure for all citizens.
prompt_hi: Prastaavana (Preamble) sab naagrikon ke liye jin chaar aadarshon ko surakshit karna chahti hai, unke naam batao.
answer: Justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Match each Preamble word with its meaning: sovereign, democratic, republic, secular, socialist.
prompt_hi: Prastaavana ke har shabd ko uske arth se milao: sovereign (samprabhu), democratic, republic, secular, socialist.
answer: Sovereign – India makes its own decisions, free of outside control; democratic – people choose their government; republic – the head of state is elected, not a hereditary monarch; secular – the state treats all religions equally and has no official religion; socialist – aims to reduce inequality so wealth and opportunity are shared more fairly.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Why does the Preamble begin with the words "We, the people of India"?
prompt_hi: Prastaavana "Hum, Bharat ke log" shabdon se kyun shuru hoti hai?
answer: Because the Constitution gets its authority from the people themselves — the people give the Constitution to themselves; power belongs to the people, not to a king or a foreign ruler.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Find the mistake: "Because India is secular, people in India are not allowed to follow any religion."
prompt_hi: Galti pakdo: "Bharat dharmanirpeksh hai, isliye Bharat mein log koi bhi dharm nahi maan sakte."
answer: Secular in India means the state has no official religion and treats all religions equally; every person is free to follow, practise and spread any religion, or none.

subject: sst
prompt_en: Predict two problems: (a) if a constitution could never be changed, and (b) if it could be changed very easily by anyone.
prompt_hi: Do mushkilein socho: (a) agar samvidhan kabhi badla hi na ja sake, aur (b) agar koi bhi use bahut aasaani se badal sake.
answer: (a) It could not adapt to new needs (for example, adding the right to education or new rights); (b) people in power could change it for their own benefit and take away rights. That is why India allows amendments, but only through a special, careful process in Parliament.
